prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: which 3 products of each category earned the most net revenue in 2025? Use the sales rows whose order_date falls in 2025 (order_date is a UTC day). Keep exactly 3 products per category, or every product when a category has fewer than 3. When products tie on revenue, the lower product_id comes first. Return three columns, in this order: category_name, product_id and revenue, the product's 2025 net revenue. Return one row for each product kept. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, look at where the numbering restarts: the question wants 3 products in every category, not 3 in all.
A window with no group in its OVER numbers every product in one long list.
starter_sql:
WITH product_rev AS (  -- one row per product with sales in 2025
  SELECT category_name, product_id, SUM(net_revenue_eur) AS revenue
  FROM sales
  WHERE order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND order_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY category_name, product_id
),
ranked AS (  -- one row per product with sales in 2025
  SELECT category_name, product_id, revenue,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC, product_id) AS rn
  FROM product_rev
)
SELECT category_name, product_id, revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 3
why_this_works: PARTITION BY category_name restarts the number in each category, so rn <= 3 keeps 3 products per category instead of 3 in all.
